A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PINE research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including material relocated between sections.

before.justification: v2 reports original RewardBench, retrieval-augmented QA, QM9 molecule-generation and R-GSM reasoning results, alongside position-bias probes and qualitative examples.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and additionally reports qualitative pilot observations about alternative importance-score aggregation methods.

M1.justification: PINE retains bidirectional inter-document attention, causal intra-document attention and position reassignment using length-normalized attention importance. The new aggregation footnote explains the existing averaging choice rather than changing the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same RewardBench datasets, retrieval-augmented QA coverage, QM9, cleaned 95-problem R-GSM subset and VLM probes. Molecule-generation and math-task descriptions move from Section 4.1 to v3 Appendix E.2.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain vanilla inference, NIA, PCW and SP, plus the permutation and calibration evaluations described in Section 4.2. The newly cited positional-encoding work is not added as an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Reported benchmark protocols retain the same models, prompts, splits, metrics and sample counts, including 10/20-document QA and the QM9 evaluation conditions. Renaming the main table's vanilla rows to 'Vanilla (Shuffle)' clarifies shuffling already described in v2.

E4.justification: v3 Section 3.3, footnote 3, newly reports pilot comparisons of summation and maximum aggregation against averaging. This adds a limited design analysis; the attention-mask and position-reassignment ablations, error analysis and qualitative examples are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify temperature-zero generation and report point estimates. Neither adds repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests.

E6.justification: All 15 tables retain their numerical entries after matching renumbered tables, and plotted benchmark results are unchanged. The addition is qualitative: v3 reports that summation induced length bias and maximum aggregation usually performed noticeably worse than averaging, without numerical estimates.

T1.justification: Lemma 1, Theorem 1 and their reasoning are retained. The lemma proof moves from Appendix B into Section 3.3, while the induction proof remains in Appendix B. The added symmetry-principle reference supplies conceptual framing without a new formal result or derivation.

C1.justification: The contribution summary changes from 'pinpoint' to 'revisit' the causes of position bias, modestly softening the claimed diagnostic contribution. Claims about training-free PINE, document-order invariance, four-task effectiveness and RewardBench reasoning gains remain.

C2.justification: v3 adds the tentative explanation that maximum aggregation performs worse because of noise from unimportant tokens. Its conclusion drops v2's explicit statement that PINE is unsuitable for efficiency-sensitive scenarios, although the computational-cost limitation and measured overhead remain.

D1.justification: Implementation frameworks, hardware, model details, processing instructions and prompts remain unchanged. The new reproducibility statement repeats existing information and the same code URL; Appendix E.2 relocates previously disclosed experiment details.

R1.justification: v3 adds Kazemnejad et al. on positional encoding to related work and Gross on symmetry to the method discussion. These modestly broaden the positioning; other reference differences chiefly concern citation style and bibliographic metadata.

P1.justification: v3 makes limited prose refinements, explicitly explains input-output invariance, shortens the conclusion and adds a reproducibility statement and expanded acknowledgments. It moves the lemma proof into the main text and task details into the appendix while retaining the overall narrative structure.

P2.justification: Conference headers, typography and spacing change. The position-bias statistics table moves from v2 Table 1 to v3 Appendix C, Table 4, and the main results table explicitly labels shuffled rows. The six figures and underlying table structures remain substantially intact.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves clarity through the explicit invariance explanation, clearer shuffled-baseline labels and placement of the existing lemma proof beside the method. The aggregation footnote provides limited additional rationale, without quantitative validation. Removing the explicit efficiency-sensitive-use warning is a small loss, but the measured overhead remains disclosed. These changes support a modest overall improvement rather than stronger scientific validation.
